title: Leaders in Base Eleven
statement:
Write every positive integer in base $11$, using digits with values $0, 1, 2, \dots, 10$. The leading digit of a positive integer is its leftmost digit in this representation, so it is never $0$.

For a positive integer $n$, let
$$L_n = \sum_{m=1}^{11^n - 1} \dfrac{1}{\ell(m)},$$
where $\ell(m)$ denotes the value of the leading digit of $m$ in base $11$.

Find the smallest positive integer $n$ for which $L_n$ is an integer.
hints: Hint 1. Group the integers below $11^n$ by their number of base-$11$ digits $k$ and by their leading digit $d$. How many have $k$ digits and leading digit $d$?

Hint 2. Each such group has $11^{k-1}$ members, so $L_n = \left(1+\frac{1}{2}+\dots+\frac{1}{10}\right)\cdot\frac{11^n-1}{10}$. The numerator of the harmonic sum is coprime to its denominator, so the problem becomes a divisibility condition on $11^n-1$. Handle each prime power with lifting the exponent or with the order of $11$.

Hint 3. The condition is $2^4\cdot 3^2\cdot 5^2\cdot 7 \mid 11^n-1$. For odd $n$ the powers of $2$ and $3$ fail. For even $n$, write $11^n-1=121^{n/2}-1$ with $121-1=120$, and lifting the exponent gives $v_2(11^n-1)=2+v_2(n)$ and $v_3(11^n-1)=1+v_3(n)$. Also $v_5(11^n-1)=1+v_5(n)$, and $11$ has order $3$ modulo $7$.
solution: The base-$11$ integers with exactly $k$ digits and leading digit $d$ are those in $[d\cdot 11^{k-1},\,(d+1)\cdot 11^{k-1})$, so there are $11^{k-1}$ of them. The integers $1,\dots,11^n-1$ are exactly those with $1$ to $n$ digits. Hence $$L_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\sum_{d=1}^{10}\dfrac{11^{k-1}}{d}=H\cdot\dfrac{11^n-1}{10},\qquad H=\sum_{d=1}^{10}\dfrac{1}{d}=\dfrac{7381}{2520}.$$ Here $7381=11^2\cdot 61$ is coprime to $2520=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7$. So $L_n=\frac{7381\,(11^n-1)}{25200}$ is an integer exactly when $25200=2^4\cdot3^2\cdot5^2\cdot7$ divides $11^n-1$. Prime $2$. If $n$ is odd, then $11^n\equiv 3^n\equiv 3\pmod 4$, so $v_2(11^n-1)=1$. If $n=2m$, then $11^n-1=121^m-1$ with $4\mid 121-1=120$. Lifting the exponent gives $v_2=v_2(120)+v_2(m)=3+v_2(n)-1=2+v_2(n)$. The condition $v_2\ge 4$ therefore holds exactly when $4\mid n$. Prime $3$. If $n$ is odd, then $11^n\equiv 2^n\equiv 2\pmod 3$, which fails. If $n=2m$, lifting the exponent with $3\mid 120$ gives $v_3(121^m-1)=1+v_3(m)=1+v_3(n)$. The condition $v_3\ge 2$ therefore holds exactly when $n$ is even and $3\mid n$. Prime $5$. Since $5\mid 11-1$, lifting the exponent gives $v_5(11^n-1)=v_5(10)+v_5(n)=1+v_5(n)$. The condition $v_5\ge 2$ holds exactly when $5\mid n$. Prime $7$. We have $11\equiv 4\pmod 7$ with $4^3=64\equiv1$ and $4\not\equiv 1$, so $11$ has order $3$ modulo $7$. Hence $7\mid 11^n-1$ exactly when $3\mid n$. Together, $25200\mid 11^n-1$ holds exactly when $4\mid n$, $3\mid n$ and $5\mid n$, that is, when $60\mid n$. The smallest such $n$ is $60$.
